caption: The drawing consists of several technical illustrations of a chair, done in black ink or pencil on a yellowed or beige background, which gives the appearance of aged paper. At the top of the page, handwritten text reads “MET. MUSEUM AMERICAN WING” and “SCALE 1/2" = 1'–0"”. The drawing is composed of four main sections: the “FRONT ELEVATION” shows the front view of the chair with detailed curved legs, a shaped seat, and an ornately cut double-splat backrest, with dimensions marked for the seat width (14 3/4 inches), overall height (41 1/2 inches to the top), and other parts; the “SIDE ELEVATION” gives the profile of the chair, detailing the curvature of the back legs, the horizontal seat rails, and the overall depth (21 inches), as well as the side angle of the seat and back. The “PLAN” view is a top-down illustration showing the seat’s shape, displaying the width at the rear (20 3/4 inches) and front (23 1/2 inches), with leg outlines at the corners and the curved edge of the seat. In the lower right corner, there is a “DETAIL NOT SCALED” section showing a close-up of the joinery of the legs and stretchers, specifically focusing on the connection and structure near a ball-and-claw foot. The entire drawing is annotated with measurements and labels, and dark spots or stains are visible along the edges, particularly in the upper right corner, contributing to the aged appearance.
title: Side Chair
